newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine judge holds 22 ex-Mendoza bank officials.
newsitem.headline: Argentine judge holds 22 ex-Mendoza bank officials.

text.p: An Argentine judge who is investigating alleged corruption in the former state bank of Mendoza province began Monday to question 22 ex-officials who were arrested in dawn raids Sunday, local officials said.

Federal Judge Luis Alberto Leiva, who has been looking at graft allegations in the Banco de Mendoza since August, had the former officials arrested over on suspicion of "economic subversion" for alleged irregularities in loan decisions.

Mendoza's current Peronist governor, Arturo Lafalla, said he would "collaborate with the courts" in its investigation of the 22 persons, appointed from 1987-95 by his Peronist predecessors Jose Octavio Bordon -- who ran for president in 1995 for a center-left coalition -- and Rodolfo Gabrielli.

Bordon and Gabrielli have been under investigation in a federal judicial probe of alleged graft in a $30 million contract won by the local branch of International Business Machines to computerize local government.

But Bordon said he was suspicious of "the spectacular nature of these arrests" in which 90 police and 35 gendarmes took part. He pledged to stand by his former employees unless they were proven guilty, saying "I know that I am honest and I am not going to run."

The Banco de Mendoza and the provincial Banco de Prevision Social have both been privatized for a total of $30 million, and will be handed over Saturday to their new owners, Magna Inversiones and Banco Republica.
